transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-26
Time: 15:00-15:45 UTC
Recorded by: Fireflies.ai
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samantha Lee (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Asha Patel (Hightower Head of ML), Marcus Reid (Platform), Diane Fox (Product)

Summary:
Quick weekly check-in on the pilot economics; focused on tradeoffs between batching window, cache hit rates, and perceived latency impact for user-facing flows. Agreement to run a 24h benchmark with KV/prefix cache enabled and to provide a pricing update that includes cache-hit tiers.

Topics covered:
- Current throughput & tokens/sec/$ observed in pilot
- Caching (prefix vs KV) observed savings and edge cases
- Batching windows and tail latency effects
- Model variant fallback behavior when capacity constrained
- Next steps and owners

Transcript body:
00:00 Speaker 1 (Samantha): Hi everyone, thanks for joining, maybe let's do a quick roll call and then Diego will walk through the latest bench results we ran overnight.
00:12 Speaker 2 (Asha): Hi, Asha here. Marcus and Diane are on.
00:15 Speaker 3 (Marcus): Marcus, yep.
:18 Speaker 4 (Diane): Diane here, thanks.
00:20 Speaker 1 (Samantha): Cool. Diego, over to you.
00:24 Speaker 5 (Diego): Yeah, thanks. So, ran the 6-hour and 24-hour runs, focused on the two main arms we discussed: cache off vs KV prefix cache on, and three batching window settings; small, medium, large — essentially 20ms/50ms/100ms. The headline — we saw roughly 2.6x tokens per dollar when cache hit rates hit ~46% on the KV setup versus cache off.
00:52 Speaker 2 (Asha): Sorry, quick clarify — 46% what exactly? 46% of requests hit the cache?
00:57 Speaker 5 (Diego): Yeah, 46% of full-token responses were served from the KV cache (prefix matches) so those avoid full cross-attention compute on the GPU. Which maps to about a 60% reduction in GPU token compute costs for those requests.
01:12 Speaker 3 (Marcus): That's really good. Did you use the same prompt distribution as prod? We worried that our confirmation dialogs might not cache well.
01:20 Speaker 5 (Diego): Good call. We used the prompt set Asha sent yesterday — we tried to be conservative but agreed some of the shorter confirm prompts had lower hit rates. We also simulated interleaving user sessions which reduced prefix reuse a bit.
01:33 Speaker 2 (Asha): Right, so the hits are uneven across flows. Product chat flow was about 55% hit rate, on boarding confirmations like the 1–3 sentence templates were like 12%.
01:45 Speaker 5 (Diego): Exactly. So overall average sits mid-40s.
01:50 Speaker 1 (Samantha): And batching tradeoffs? How's P95?
01:54 Speaker 5 (Diego): With small batch (20ms) P95 was ~210ms, medium (50ms) P95 went to 300ms, large (100ms) P95 jumped to ~470ms — but tokens/sec/$ improved noticeably: small gave baseline cost X, medium ~1.3X tokens per dollar, large ~1.8X. There's a steep tail cost for the 100ms window when you have many short queries, obviously.
02:20 Speaker 4 (Diane): So product is sensitive to P95 under 300 for the user chat flow. Anything over and it feels laggy to users.
02:27 Speaker 5 (Diego): Yep, that's consistent with what we saw. For the product chat path, medium seems like the sweet spot — 50ms gives decent lift without pushing P95 past 300ms when prefix cache is hitting at least 30%.
02:40 Speaker 2 (Asha): Quick question on cache invalidation — if a user updates profile data mid-conversation, will prefix cache return stale content?
02:48 Speaker 5 (Diego): Good question. In the current pilot config we scope cache keys to message prefix hashes plus user-scoped TTLs. If you update profile fields that alter prompt template variables, we recommend client-side cache bust or using a short TTL for those keys. We can show config snippets.
03:05 Speaker 1 (Samantha): We'll include sample snippet in the follow-up email.
03:08 Speaker 3 (Marcus): Another ops question — memory on the serving nodes when KV cache is enabled, did you observe any OOMs or swapping?
03:16 Speaker 5 (Diego): No OOMs at the tested scale. We used LRU eviction and capped the KV store at 30GB per node, and observed normal memory footprint. If you push to more concurrent users, we'd scale nodes or prefer a shared external cache option.
03:30 Speaker 2 (Asha): About fallback behavior: what happens when dedicated capacity is saturated — do you fallback to a smaller quantized model or queue requests?
03:37 Speaker 5 (Diego): By default we have smart routing — the policy we used was latency-first, then cost. So when capacity hits a threshold, requests fall back to a compatible lower-memory model variant (we used model-x-quant) for non-critical routes, and for critical routes the request is queued briefly and re-routed. We can tune policy per route.
03:55 Speaker 4 (Diane): That routing change would need to be approved by product since some of our safety checks rely on model behavior.
04:02 Speaker 5 (Diego): Understood — we can set an explicit route label that opts out of fallbacks.
04:06 Speaker 1 (Samantha): Pricing — we said we would send a revised pilot pricing with cache hit tiers. Diego, any number guidance from the runs?
04:13 Speaker 5 (Diego): From the 24-hour run, at 40–50% cache hit we see token efficiency of about 2.4x–2.8x; we'd propose a tiered pilot credit model: base unit price for cache-miss tokens and a reduced unit for cache-hit tokens, plus a small per-node overhead. Samantha will finalize numbers.
04:32 Speaker 2 (Asha): That would help, yes. Also can you show per-route cost breakdowns? We need to see which flows consume the most tokens per success metric.
04:40 Speaker 5 (Diego): We have per-route token logs from the pilot — will include CSV and a short pivot that maps flows to tokens per successful action.
04:47 Speaker 3 (Marcus): On the benchmarking — will you simulate realistic concurrency? Our peak is ~480 req/minute with burstiness.
04:54 Speaker 5 (Diego): We did a few burst tests at that scale, but Diego continues: the 24h run had synthetic diurnal patterns, but we'll re-run with the exact 480 r/min peak profile and include a 2x burst subtest.
05:08 Speaker 2 (Asha): Great. Anything else on caching edge cases?
05:12 Speaker 5 (Diego): One other gotcha — prompt paraphrasing reduces prefix hits; we saw up to 15% lower hit rate when paraphrase variants were common. There's an opportunity to augment with lightweight semantic fingerprinting to cluster paraphrases into same key, but that's extra complexity.
05:30 Speaker 4 (Diane): That sounds like a feature ask — might be a next-phase improvement. For now, we need clarity on expected savings for the current prompt set.
05:39 Speaker 1 (Samantha): Right. So agreed action: Diego run the 24h with KV enabled and the exact prod-like burst profile; Asha send final prompt set; Samantha send pricing update.
05:50 Speaker 2 (Asha): We'll send the 50 canonical prompts and the few short confirmation templates — expect that after the call.
05:57 Speaker 3 (Marcus): Can we also get a run where batching is adaptive — if load low, we wait longer to fill batch, if load high, reduce the window? Is that supported?
06:06 Speaker 5 (Diego): Redwood runtime supports adaptive batching policies. We didn't enable it in this run to keep experiments controlled, but we can enable in the next run. It tends to give the best of both worlds if your latency SLOs can tolerate small increases at low load.
06:22 Speaker 1 (Samantha): Ok, Diego will add adaptive batching to one of the 24h subtests.
06:27 Speaker 5 (Diego): Yep, will do.
06:29 Speaker 2 (Asha): On security/compliance — team had a few Qs last week about audit logs when cache is enabled, does that change log contents?
06:37 Speaker 5 (Diego): No changes to audit events. We still emit request and response IDs and route metadata. The KV cache only affects execution path; logs still show whether a response was served from cache or compute.
06:48 Speaker 4 (Diane): And for private deployments — if we move to VPC, is the KV store inside the customer's network?
06:54 Speaker 5 (Diego): For private we can run the KV store as a customer-managed service inside the VPC or use an on-prem Redis that you control. That is part of the Private deployment conversation.
07:04 Speaker 1 (Samantha): Alright, any blockers before we wrap?
07:08 Speaker 2 (Asha): No blockers. Just want the clarity in the pricing email and the benchmark by EOM.
07:14 Speaker 3 (Marcus): No blockers from infra — we can supply exact traffic profile CSV.
07:18 Speaker 1 (Samantha): Great. Thanks everyone. We'll share results and schedule the on-prem deep dive for the week of April 6th.
07:26 Speaker 2 (Asha): Thanks.
07:28 Speaker 5 (Diego): Thanks all.
07:30 End of meeting.
